user.title: Calibrate a light
user.description:
Pick a light you trust as the reference, and the light that doesn't match it.

This creates a calibrated light that takes over the target's entity ID, so everything already pointing at that light keeps working and gets corrected output. The real fixture is renamed with a `_raw` suffix and hidden.

Tunable-white lights can be calibrated too -- they get colour temperature and brightness, but not tint or colours, which they have no way to show.

Pick a reference that covers the colour temperatures you care about -- steps it can't reach are skipped rather than measured wrongly.

Calibration starts as soon as this is created.

data.reference_entity: Reference light (the one that looks right)
data.name: Name (optional)

error.same_light: The reference and the light being calibrated have to be two different lights.
error.not_registered: That light can't be taken over. The calibrated light claims its entity ID, so Home Assistant has to be able to rename the original -- a YAML light or a light group can't be renamed. Pick a light that came from an integration.
error.raw_light: That's the real fixture behind a light that's already calibrated. Pick the calibrated light instead, or a different one.
error.already_calibrated: That light is already calibrated. Open its Configure page to re-run or fine-tune it.
error.no_color_control: That light has no colour control at all -- it can't be set to a colour or a colour temperature, so there's nothing to calibrate.

create_entry.default:
**[Start calibrating →](/light-calibration)**

That opens the guided matching straight away -- pick how thorough you want to be and the sliders take over from there.

Pause anything that adapts these lights automatically first, or it will re-adapt them while you work. You can also get back here any time from this entry's **Configure** button.
